scope: Evaluate only whether PAR-, VAM-/VAMA- and SAR- should be governed as nonproductive analytical semantic clusters. Do not create standalone roots, new derived words, lexical meanings, grammar, productivity or curriculum changes.

families.semantic_observation: The forms cluster around study/school, library, study/action and seeing/perception, giving a learning/knowledge/perception association stronger than the other broad families.
families.boundary: Internal PAR segmentation is not historically recovered. B8 governs only the closed PARAZAMO/PARAZAMI pair; that does not make PAR- a root or productive morpheme.

families.semantic_observation: Several forms touch identity, preference, leisure or personal activity, but the semantic range is broad and the surface prefix is not uniform across VAMA-, VAMU- and VAME.
families.boundary: Do not normalize these forms to a single VAM root and do not derive new personal-domain vocabulary from the cluster.

families.semantic_observation: Known meanings span origin, time/duration, travel and habituality and can be descriptively grouped as a broad spacetime/trajectory family, but the grouping is too broad to establish a semantic primitive.
families.boundary: SAROSAL remains without recovered gloss. Do not infer its meaning from the family and do not derive temporal, spatial or trajectory vocabulary from SAR-.

anti_oversegmentation_evidence.finding: Recurring surface strings cross semantic families, so substring recurrence alone cannot establish a morpheme.

options.effect: Govern PAR-, VAM-/VAMA- and SAR- as descriptive analytical families with explicit confidence levels and zero derivational productivity.
Retain the audit observations but do not give the clusters any governed analytical status.
